newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian Socialists appeal election ruling.
newsitem.headline: Serbian Socialists appeal election ruling.

text.p: A Serbian court said on Monday the government and an allied radical party had appealed against an electoral commission ruling that awarded victory to the opposition in Belgrade local elections two months ago.
The Belgrade municipal court announced that it would ask the Serbian Supreme Court to decide what level of the judicial system should rule on the appeals.

It said two appeals were submitted -- one by President Slobodan Milosevic's Socialists (SPS) and the other by the rightist Serbian Radical Party (SRS), which is not in the government but opposes Serbia's moderate opposition coalition.
The appeal in Belgrade was lodged in the ninth week of pro-democracy demonstrations against the government's annulment of Serbia-wide municipal voting won by the opposition bloc.

The electoral commission in Nis, Serbia's second largest city, declared an opposition victory there as well last week. An SPS appeal was thrown out by Nis municipal court and Zajedno said it would convene the new regional assembly on January 27.
